bull.b: Retiring $50M of convertible debt and holding material cash/marketable securities meaningfully reduces near‑term solvency and refinancing risk. This strengthened balance sheet and >12 months runway support execution of product rollouts and partnership integrations while the business scales AUM and revenue.

bull.t: Live product with operational proof points
bull.b: A live, yield‑bearing token that has paid dividends and shows NAV tracking establishes operational credibility; an independent attestation in process adds auditability. These durable product foundations are necessary for scaling AUM, monetizing fees, and converting technical infrastructure into recurring revenue as distribution expands.

bull.t: Institutional partnerships improving distribution and liquidity
bull.b: Partnerships with market makers, a permissioned secondary market, and a major IRA custodian materially lower distribution friction and enhance liquidity prospects. These structural ties increase likelihood of AUM scale, recurring fee capture, and differentiation versus peers lacking integrated custodial and market‑making channels.

bear.t: No GAAP revenue and weak profitability
bear.b: Zero GAAP revenue and persistent net losses indicate the company has yet to validate its commercial model at scale. Until revenue and margins materialize, the business will struggle to convert product proof points into self‑sustaining economics, leaving structural execution risk and dependence on sustained capital support.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow forces reliance on financing and asset monetization until product revenue scales. Even with current cash and securities, runway depends on execution; sustained cash burn can force dilutive raises or curtailed growth if AUM ramps slower than forecast.

bear.t: High non‑cash stock compensation and governance dilution risk
bear.b: Material equity‑based pay and large restricted/ performance grants inflate reported expenses and create future dilution pressure as milestones are achieved or severance triggers occur. This raises long‑term shareholder dilution risk and may misalign incentives if compensation focuses on lofty valuation targets rather than steady, sustainable AUM economics.
